reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.referenceIntensity
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: the intensity dt nu(de) of N on R_+ x E. Faithful Lean: the product measure
(Lebesgue on the time half-line) x nu on (time) x E: volume on NNReal (or Lebesgue restricted to
[0,infinity) on R) times nu, as Measure.prod. If the time axis is all of R with full Lebesgue,
that is a PRM on R x E; harmless only if every use (filtration, integral, PRM) is restricted to
nonnegative times consistently. The order of factors (time x E vs E x time) must match the
random measure's space. Both factors sigma-finite (nu sigma-finite by the setting) so that the
product is the unique product measure.

comparison.text:
Lean: referenceIntensity nu : Measure (R x E) := (volume.restrict (Set.Ici 0)).prod nu.
Comparison with the locked reading: the product of Lebesgue measure on the time half-line [0,inf)
with nu, factors in the order (time x E) matching N : Omega -> Measure (R x E); Measure.prod is the
standard product (unique since both factors are sigma-finite: Lebesgue restricted is sigma-finite,
nu sigma-finite where the PRM uses it). Representation choice: the time axis is all of R with the
restricted Lebesgue measure, so negative-time regions have intensity 0; this is used consistently
(the PRM, the filtrations indexed by R, the integral vanishing for t <= 0), as the reading
required for harmlessness. (For a region {0} x E with nu(E) = infinity, the intensity is 0 * top =
0 in ENNReal, correct.)

verdict.detail:
Representation choice: the time axis is all of R with Lebesgue restricted to [0,inf), so
negative-time regions have intensity 0; used consistently by the PRM (on R x E), the filtrations
(indexed by R) and the integral (0 for t <= 0). Restricted to [0,inf) x E it is dt nu(de).

author_review.disagreements:
Minor, classification only: the author records "faithful"; I record "faithful with
representation choices" because the measure lives on R x E (Lebesgue restricted to [0,inf) times
nu) rather than on R_+ x E; used consistently by the PRM, the filtrations and the integral, so
harmless. No substantive disagreement.
